archetype: Ranged STR pirate artillery. Wide horizontal area attacks and a summoned monkey; high mobility from Monkey Push/Boost plus Cannon Jump. Job path is Cannoneer (2nd) -> Cannon Trooper (3rd) -> Cannon Master (4th); the class is picked directly at character creation rather than advanced into through the generic Pirate line. Job advancement quests unlock at Lv. 10 / 30 / 60 / 100, 5th job at Lv. 200, 6th job at Lv. 260.

linkSkill.name: Pirate's Blessing
linkSkill.effect: At master level: STR +100, DEX +100, INT +100, LUK +100, Max HP +1750, Max MP +1750, Damage Taken -21%. Stacks up to 3 times, once per unique Explorer Pirate that reaches master level. Values scale with %Stat effects. On Explorer Pirates the skill can be double-clicked to toggle a mode that swaps STR+%STR and DEX+%DEX granted by equipment; primary weapon, secondary weapon, totems and symbols are excluded.
linkSkill.note: MapleStory Wiki names it 'Pirate Blessing' without the apostrophe-s; Grandis Library names it 'Pirate's Blessing'. Same skill. Pre-revamp guides list obsolete values - see conflicts.

vMatrix.notes: RECENCY POINT THAT MATTERS. Boost nodes were restructured in GMS v.269; Grandis Library presents the fixed node groups above as current and keeps the old layout behind a separate 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle. Any guide telling you to craft specific three-skill trios is describing the pre-v.269 system. The 2024 DigitalTQ guide, for instance, recommends the trios [Cannon Barrage / Rolling Rainbow / Monkey Militia] and [Cannon Bazooka / Monkey Fury / Anchors Away]; those are recorded here only as superseded history, not as current advice. No post-v.269 source was found that ranks the six node groups against each other, and Grandis Library's own tier colouring could not be extracted as text, so no ranked build order is asserted. The Cannoneer class Discord (https://discord.gg/XJzkgQRPcM) is the maintainer Grandis Library credits for these builds and is where the ranking would come from.

hexa.notes: NOT SOURCED for Cannoneer specifically. No guide dated after the HEXA rollout was found that gives a Cannoneer investment order across origin skill core, mastery cores, enhancement/boost cores and common cores. Left null deliberately - misallocated Sol Erda is expensive to undo. What IS sourced: (1) Cannoneer's 6th job origin skill is Super Cannon Explosion, which doubles as the class's bind (10s duration, 360s cooldown) and carries an iFrame [Grandis Library]. (2) HEXA counterparts named for this class on the skill wiki include HEXA Cannon Barrage, HEXA Cannon Bazooka, HEXA Anchors Aweigh, HEXA Nautilus Strike, HEXA Monkey Mortar, HEXA Rolling Rainbow, HEXA Support Monkey and HEXA Monkey Fury [MapleStory Wiki]. (3) A class-agnostic HEXA guide updated 2025-01-31 recommends activating the 6th job mastery node, then boost nodes, then the origin skill node, then common nodes, leaving HEXA Stat until skills are at a decent level, reasoning that spreading activations across nodes beats levelling one node and that HEXA Stat returns less final damage per resource early [The Digital Crowns]. That is generic and is NOT a Cannoneer recommendation - a placeholder only, and it conflicts with the origin-skill-first ordering commonly repeated in the community, which no datable source in this pass could be found to support.

hyperStats.notes: No Cannoneer-specific hyper stat priority was found in any source in this pass. The list above is a general STR-bossing order from a class-agnostic hyper stat guide last updated 2026-08-19, annotated with Cannoneer's own passive totals so the reader can see where the class already has coverage. Present it as a starting frame, never as a class build.

bossingPassives.note: Grandis Library credits this build to the Cannoneer Discord, so this is one source chain, not two.

The 2024 DigitalTQ guide additionally lists Rolling Rainbow, Epic Adventure and Buckshot among its recommendations; the v.269 Grandis Library build does not include them in the passive selection. No source found in this pass covers the hyper active or hyper stat hyper skill choices for this class, so activeHypers is left null rather than guessed.

bossing.why: Top line for bossing. The Hand Cannon is slow at base and the class spends five passive skills' worth of bonuses climbing out of it, so the remaining stage is valuable. This is the one inner ability line every Cannoneer source agrees on, across a twelve-year span of guides.
Second and third lines for a bossing set-up.

bossing.line: Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status +8%
bossing.why: Second and third lines for a bossing set-up.

training.why: Farming set-up; throughput matters more than damage once mobs die in one hit.

innerAbility.notes: The bossing second and third lines and the whole training set come from Grandis Library, which credits the Cannoneer Discord - one chain. Only the Attack Speed +1 line is corroborated independently. The 2013 AyumiLove entry pairs Attack Speed +1 with Attack +30, which is a pre-modern second line and should not be shown as current.

gearingNotes: Cannoneer gears as a STR Explorer Pirate: Hand Cannon in the weapon slot, Powder Keg as the secondary, pirate-class armour, STR main and DEX secondary. Grandis Library records a 1.5x weapon multiplier and 85% weapon mastery from the kit. Two things in the kit should change what you buy. First, the class already carries +45% critical rate and +29% boss damage before any gear, and +20% ignore DEF rising to +40% with its conditional sources - so crit rate lines are worth less on this class than on one starting near zero, and early IED and boss damage stack onto an existing base. Second, the Hand Cannon is slow at base and the class climbs five attack speed stages back through Agile Cannons, Reinforced Cannon, Cannon Overload and Buckshot, which is why Attack Speed +1 is the recommended inner ability first line rather than a damage line. Pirate's Blessing carries an Explorer-Pirate-only toggle that swaps STR and DEX granted by equipment (weapons, totems and symbols excluded), which is what lets a Cannoneer make use of gear rolled for the other stat. NO SOURCE was found in this pass for Cannoneer-specific set choices - Arcane/Genesis/Eternal progression, Pitched Boss pieces, familiar lines, or Heroic-server meso and drop gearing - so none is asserted.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning a party around Cannoneer's dice buffs
commonMistakes.why: Roll of the Dice and Double Down are random, so the party buff a Cannoneer contributes is not something to count on.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
defects: UNSOURCED PRIORITY ORDER - the main defect. Grandis Library DOES state the boost node tiers in text, not only as colour coding. I confirmed across three separately-worded fetches: legend reads "Each Boost Node provides a %Final Damage increase to the skills included in the node. Nodes categorized as Primary and Secondary are recommended to be upgraded", with Node 1 = PRIMARY, Node 2 = SECONDARY, Nodes 3, 4, 5 and 6 ALL = OTHER. So (a) vMatrix.priority[0].why ("the exact ranking between the six groups is NOT sourced here"), priority[4].why and priority[5].why ("Tier assignment NOT sourced") and vMatrix.notes ("No post-v.269 source was found that ranks the six node groups against each other") are each FALSE - the researcher quoted the legend's Primary definition while claiming the assignment was unreadable; and (b) the file's 1-through-6 array ordering implies groups 3 > 4 > 5 > 6, a rank NO source states, since GL flattens all four into OTHER. That implied order is exactly the invented-priority failure mode.

EIGHT HEXA NODE NAMES REST ON A PAGE NOBODY OPENED. "HEXA Cannon Barrage, HEXA Cannon Bazooka, HEXA Anchors Aweigh, HEXA Nautilus Strike, HEXA Monkey Mortar, HEXA Rolling Rainbow, HEXA Support Monkey, HEXA Monkey Fury" come solely from search-engine snippets of maplestorywiki.net/w/Cannoneer/Skills, which 403s for me too. I could not confirm a single one. This is load-bearing: the "has a named HEXA counterpart" claim is the stated rationale for vMatrix groups 1, 2, 3 and 4 and for hexa.notes item (2). The BASE skill names are all real (verified on GL: Monkey Mortar is 3rd job, Nautilus Strike / Anchors Aweigh / Support Monkey / Cannon Barrage / Cannon Bazooka are 4th job, Monkey Fury is 3rd job, Rolling Rainbow is a Hyper Skill) - but eight HEXA masteries for one class is far more than classes typically receive, and nothing in this pass substantiates it. Treat as unverified, not confirmed.

SELF-DEFEATING RATIONALE. vMatrix.priority[0].why argues Cannon Barrage is top-bracket BECAUSE it "has a named HEXA counterpart" - but the file then asserts named HEXA counterparts for groups 2, 3 and 4 as well. The criterion does not discriminate, so the reasoning chain does not actually support the ordering it is offered for. This is inference standing in for a source label that was available on the page.

"Monkey Militia" is carried in vMatrix.notes and conflicts[0] as a DigitalTQ trio member with no note that the skill name no longer exists. GL's current skill list has no Monkey Militia anywhere (the monkey skills are Monkey Magic, Monkey Mortar, Monkey Fury, Mega Monkey Magic, Support Monkey, Monkey Business). A reader searching the name in-game finds nothing. Same problem with the spelling drift: the file uses "Anchors Aweigh" (correct, verified on GL) in vMatrix.priority and "Anchors Away" (DigitalTQ's spelling) in vMatrix.notes and conflicts[0] without flagging that one is a misspelling of the other.

No outright invented node or skill name found otherwise. Every skill in all six boost node groups matches GL's skill list exactly, group membership matches verbatim, both hyper passive builds match GL verbatim, both inner ability sets match GL, Super Cannon Explosion is confirmed as the 6th job origin skill, Powder Keg is confirmed as secondary, and the "View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes" toggle exists with that exact label. hexa.order being null is correct - I confirmed GL states no HEXA investment order, only the legend phrase "Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used".

STALE: AYUMILOVE IS MISCHARACTERISED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. sources[] says the 2013 page is "STALE - predates 5th job, V matrix and HEXA entirely" and that the v1 page "contains none" of V matrix content. Two separately-worded fetches of ayumilove.net/maplestory-cannon-shooter-skill-build-guide/ both report a V-Matrix / 5th job section in the body with a main V skill and trio recommendations. AyumiLove updates pages in place while keeping the original post date, so the "2013-04-06" stamp is a publication date, not a content date. Consequence: the file simultaneously over-trusts that stamp (using it as a "twelve-year span" corroboration for Attack Speed +1) and over-dismisses the page (declaring its V matrix content nonexistent). Caveat on my own check: the V skill name returned ("Gigantic Cannonball") does not appear in GL's 5th job list (Cannon of Mass Destruction, Monkey Business, Poolmaker, Pirate's Banner, Loaded Dice, Overdrive, Maple World Goddess's Blessing), so either AyumiLove's own V section is stale or the extraction is unreliable - but "contains no V matrix content" is not right either way.

STALE: DIGITALTQ DATING IS RIGHT BUT GENEROUS. I confirmed the visible dates: "February 19, 2024" publication, changelog "06/03/2023 - Updated for Destiny Remastered Patch", "26/03/2021 - Added new 5th Job Skill from the Awake update", "16/11/2020 - First update", footer "(c) Copyright 2026". So the newest CONTENT revision is 2023-06-03, not 2024-02-19; the file's "2024-02-19 article date" reads fresher than the guide is. The file's conclusion (pre-v.269, superseded on boost nodes) is correct and I confirmed the page references no version above Destiny Remastered.

STALE: NO pre-HEXA advice is passed off as current - this is the file's strongest quality. DigitalTQ trios and AyumiLove link values are explicitly quarantined into conflicts[] and commonMistakes[], hexa.order and vMatrix.trios and activeHypers are null rather than guessed, and the generic hyperStats import is labelled non-class-specific in three places. The residual staleness risk is disclosed rather than hidden: Grandis Library is stamped GMS v.269 [Ride the Lightning Update] (verified verbatim) against the file's v.271 target, i.e. two patches behind, and nothing in this pass covers what v.270 or v.271 changed for this class.

STALE: RECENCY FLOOR NOT MET IN SUBSTANCE. The brief asks for sources after 2025-01-01. Of the four Cannoneer-specific chains, zero carry a 2025-or-later date: GL has a version stamp only, the wiki is undated and unreadable, DigitalTQ's content is 2023, AyumiLove's stamp is 2013. The only two post-2025-dated sources in the file (The Digital Crowns 2025-01-31, GamesLikeFinder 2026-08-19) are both class-agnostic. The file's coverageWarnings say this, but consensusLevel "weak" undersells it - for V MATRIX, HEXA, HYPER STATS and GEARING there is effectively one datable class-specific source chain.
